solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Youngster half-heartedly declines berries

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout

indicators.note: the word's heart is its doubled middle pair, and half of that pair goes

parts.note: ebbs means falls away or declines

explanation.surface: A child half-heartedly turns down an offer of berries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two central Bs of EBBS, leaving EBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubebs are the small pungent berries of a pepper plant, used as a spice.

clue.text: Top brass

definitions.meaning: the top of the head or of a hill
brass is slang for money, and a ... was an old British coin worth five shillings

explanation.surface: Reads as the senior officers of an army.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'top brass' wants to be read as one idea, but it splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown is both the highest point of something and an old coin, coins being 'brass' in slang.

clue.text: ABBA's ignoring Björk's tip to boogie with Tim Rice

indicators.note: to boogie is to dance about, so the letters are jumbled
ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is removed from the group's name

parts.note: the Swedish pop group's name with its 's, taken as letters

indicators.note: the tip of the singer's name is its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pop trivia: ABBA dancing with lyricist Tim Rice, minus a nod to Björk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes one B (Björk's tip) from ABBAS, leaving ABAS; 'to boogie' shuffles ABAS with TIM. 'Tim Rice' looks like one name; the surname is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a long-grained, fragrant variety of rice grown in India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Fool and Fairy Queen upset drink over Will's Bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, i.e. reads it backwards

parts.note: Queen Mab is the fairy queen of English folklore, described in Romeo and Juliet

indicators.note: over means covering, so the drink word goes round the other piece

parts.note: booze means alcoholic drink

indicators.note: Bottom here means the end of the word, its final letter, playing on Shakespeare's weaver

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean scene: the fairy queen Titania doting on Bottom, the weaver given an ass's head in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the queen's name backwards in this down clue, and 'over' wraps the drink round the final letter of Will (Shakespeare). Bottom looks like the character but means the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bamboozle someone is to trick or deceive them, i.e. make a fool of them.

clue.text: Poke fun at Steffi's second service

parts.note: to tease is to poke fun at someone

indicators.note: second picks the letter in position two of the tennis player's name

explanation.surface: Mocking Steffi Graf's second serve at tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a tennis serve, after Steffi Graf, but it means a set of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea service is the matching set of cups, saucers and pot used for serving tea.

clue.text: Measurement unit always abbreviated in ruler

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of measurement

indicators.note: abbreviated means shortened, as in the poetic contraction that drops a letter

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A metric unit that always gets shortened on a measuring ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abbreviated' turns EVER into the poetic E'ER. 'ruler' suggests a measuring stick, but it is a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeer (emir) is a Muslim prince or commander, a ruler of an emirate.

clue.text: Carrier pigeons at Chelsea billets

indicators.note: to billet is to lodge or house, so these words lodge the answer within them

explanation.surface: Carrier pigeons being lodged at Chelsea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrier' seems to go with 'pigeons', but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a bag with a strap for carrying books, so a carrier in the sense of a bag.

clue.text: Spinner's trajectory is outstanding

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy, so the spinner's (belonging to it) gives top
a flight is the path a ball travels through the air

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler's flight being superb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket spin bowler, whose 'flight' is the loop of the ball, but it is a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest class, i.e. excellent or outstanding.

clue.text: Swallow, rook and other birds heading west

parts.note: to rook someone is to swindle or con them

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's list: a swallow, a rook and others flying west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' reverses the flightless birds. 'Swallow' and 'rook' both look like birds, but one is the definition (a verb) and the other means swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume is to eat or drink, so to swallow.

clue.text: Police lacking power to stop page being edited

indicators.note: being edited means being reworked, so the letters are rearranged
lacking means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A police order to halt a page of print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes a P from STOPPAGE, leaving STOPAGE; 'being edited' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: Japanese leader's lurking in the wings here

definitions.text: Japanese leader's lurking in the wings here

parts.words: Japanese leader's lurking in the wings here
parts.note: the emperor of Japan's title doubles as the name of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, whose performers wait in the theatre wings

explanation.surface: The emperor of Japan is hiding offstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wings' are the offstage sides of a theatre, so 'here' is a stage show named after the Japanese leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is an 1885 Gilbert and Sullivan operetta set in Japan, named for its emperor.

clue.text: See 12
Following realignment, no real hope then for Mutual Assistance Directive

indicators.note: after realignment the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A bleak verdict on an EU-style directive after political realignment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an instruction (a directive) that people assist each other, i.e. mutual aid.

clue.text: Possible bad hair day? Sleep on it

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the first piece

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
zz represents snoring, so sleep

explanation.surface: Having a bad hair day? Advice to sleep on the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad hair day' reads as a single phrase, but 'day' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Frizz is tightly curled, fuzzy hair, the kind that can ruin someone's appearance.

clue.text: Changes policy following spin failures

parts.note: to flip is to turn or spin over
flops are failures

explanation.surface: A government does a U-turn after its spin doctoring fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' looks like political spin, but it means a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip-flop is to reverse one's stated position, typical of a politician.

clue.text: Gum Alice mixed is sticky stuff

indicators.note: mixed means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Alice mixing gum, which turns out sticky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gum' looks like the definition, but it is part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucilage is a thick gluey substance from plants, used as an adhesive.

clue.text: Junior sailors about to reject marks for navigating in sound

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
to bin something is to throw it away or reject it

indicators.note: in sound means as heard, so the word is spelt as it is said

parts.note: buoys are floating markers that guide ships

explanation.surface: Junior sailors about to refuse navigation buoys in a sea inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a stretch of water, but signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabin boys were young lads serving the officers and passengers aboard a ship.

clue.text: Teacher's pet heard to use words wrongly

indicators.note: heard means said out loud, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: Miss is how pupils address a teacher, here with a possessive; a pet is a fit of pique or sulking

explanation.surface: A teacher's favourite pupil heard using words wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's pet' looks like a favourite pupil; it is 'Miss's pique', a teacher's sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: To misspeak is to say something incorrectly or not as intended.

clue.text: High level view of broadcaster's policy

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
a line is an official policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: An overview of a TV channel's editorial policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyline is the outline of buildings seen against the sky, literally a view at a high level.

clue.text: Cry from blackface leaving fold?

parts.note: a Blackface is a breed of sheep, and a sheep straying from its pen would call out

explanation.surface: A noise from a sheep straying from its pen.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scottish Blackface is a hardy hill-sheep breed; 'blackface' also suggests a minstrel act, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleat is the plaintive cry of a sheep or goat.

clue.text: Doctor suffocated by record high temperature losing footing in arid bush

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: suffocated by means enclosed by, so this piece is wrapped inside
losing its footing means losing its bottom letter in a down clue

parts.note: heat means a high temperature

explanation.surface: A doctor overcome by heat, falling over in desert scrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing footing' drops the last letter of the temperature word (the bottom, in a down clue), giving HEA, and 'suffocated by' buries the doctor inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephedra is a genus of jointed shrubs of dry regions, source of the drug ephedrine.

clue.text: Lose head in no time? Not sure

indicators.note: losing its head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: in a jiffy means in no time, so jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper in an instant, then doubting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or uncertain.

clue.text: Adrian Chiles gutted about conveyance held up by Poles

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: gutted means losing its insides, so central letters of the surname are removed

explanation.surface: Broadcaster Adrian Chiles is devastated about a vehicle stopped by Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: Adrian Chiles is a British TV presenter. 'gutted' takes IL out of CHILES, leaving CHES; 'about' shuffles that with ADRIAN. 'Poles' looks like people from Poland, but means carrying poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on two poles by bearers.

clue.text: Trap to catch poisoner?

definitions.meaning: a police operation set up to trap criminals
the organ an insect uses to inject venom, so a poisoner of sorts

explanation.surface: A setup to catch someone who poisons people.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'poisoner' as a loose description of a wasp's or bee's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sting means both an undercover trap and the venomous barb of an insect.

clue.text: Fix papers to procure decoration

indicators.note: to procure means to obtain and hold, so the papers take the decoration inside them

parts.note: ID means identity papers
MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Forging documents to obtain an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British honour (Member of the Order of the British Empire).
explanation.definitionFit: To imbed (embed) is to fix something firmly in a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Amendment by one willing to bring retired detectives into loop

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so this piece goes within the loop

parts.note: a coil is a loop or series of loops

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: An amendment brings retired detectives back into the loop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns CID into DIC. 'one willing' is a pun: someone making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplement that adds to or alters a will already made.

clue.text: Artist concealing personal information joins company in Spanish city

indicators.note: concealing means hiding, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
DOB is date of birth, a piece of personal information

explanation.surface: An artist hiding personal details joins a firm in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Córdoba is an Andalusian city famous for its Great Mosque.

clue.text: Proclaim order to destroy vehicle

indicators.note: to proclaim is to declare out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: slay! is a command to kill or destroy

explanation.surface: A decree to wreck a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn by horses or reindeer, a vehicle for snow.

clue.text: 75% of liar's admission is key

indicators.note: taking three quarters means cutting the last quarter of the letters

parts.note: a liar might admit 'I slander'

explanation.surface: Three quarters of a liar's confession turns out to be crucial.
explanation.walkthrough: '75% of' takes six of the eight letters of I SLANDER. 'key' is not crucial but a cay, a low island.
explanation.definitionFit: A key (or cay) is a small low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys.
